question: If moment generating function of continuous random variable X is (λ)/(λ-t) t < λ, then E(X³) equals to:
solution:
The correct answer is 6/λ³

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **moment generating function (MGF)** of a random variable is a function that represents the expected values of its powers. 

 
 
• The MGF of X is defined as M(t) = E(e^(tx)), where E represents the expected value.
 
• The nth derivative of the MGF evaluated at t = 0 provides the expected value of X^n.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• To calculate E(X³) from the MGF of X, you need to take the third derivative of M(t) with respect to t, and then evaluate it at t = 0.
 
• The MGF method assumes that the random variable X has a moment generating function, which may not be the case for all distributions.
